findings.title: First cancellation after Popen handle acquisition can bypass all owned-controller wait and kill
findings.source: supervise.py:117-140, especially129 between the separate constructor and wait try blocks
findings.evidence: An independent pure-fake trace raises one KeyboardInterrupt at run_child_once line129 after the factory returned the original fake object. The exception escapes; fake process events are empty, so wait180, kill and wait5 are all absent.
findings.trigger: A first KeyboardInterrupt is delivered after a controller Popen object has been assigned but before entry into the protected wait block. The constructor and wait use separate try/except regions. That cancellation is not handled by bounded_stop.
findings.impact: The wrapper can unwind and drop the original process object without applying its180-second bound or owned-handle cleanup. A controller stuck on R4-P2-001 can survive without the intended outer containment. R4's independently repaired Job-close path is not rescinded, but the new supervisor's cancellation/lifetime guarantee is unmet.
findings.required_minimum_repair: In a new preserved revision initialize process=None before the protected region, put Popen assignment and the first wait in the same try, and distinguish construction uncertainty from an already-acquired original process in the exception handler. An acquired process must go through exactly one same-object kill and one bounded5s confirmation, remain UNKNOWN, and never be rediscovered or retried.
findings.required_regression: Inject one cancellation after returned-object assignment but before first wait, including line/opcode boundaries around acquisition. Assert no escape, same original object retained, exactly one kill plus one wait5, UNKNOWN and no RESULT loader/late promotion. Do not merely move a hard-coded line number.
findings.preservation: Keep all v1 manifest16 pins, source, tests, failed author attempt and this report unchanged. New revision may change its manifest/scope ROOT, but must retain the original global supervisor attempt-01, original R4 run-01/controller/scope/43861 and one total launch.

verified_static_boundaries: Windows-only fixed Python pin; local stdlib retains CreateProcess hp in Popen._handle, wait uses WaitForSingleObject(_handle), kill aliases TerminateProcess(_handle). Wrapper uses the returned object, no PID/name/port rediscovery or poll/context-manager join.
Fixed R4 controller/scope/review hashes and exact43861/run-01; DEVNULL on all streams, shell false, close_fds true, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, minimal fresh controller environment.
On the normal constructed-object path the first potentially blocking operation is wait(timeout180), before logs, file reads/hashes/Sync or callbacks.

A TimeoutExpired or exception delivered inside that wait calls kill exactly once on the same original object, then at most one wait(timeout5). UNKNOWN is sticky and no late RESULT is read on those paths.

Known exit0 is only eligible for bounded public RESULT parsing and complete reported-proof checks. Missing/malformed/incomplete/nonzero evidence is inconclusive. Complete reported proof remains ROOT_REVIEW_REQUIRED, resource_ready false and not independent acceptance.

Prelaunch pins bind an exact public D receipt Root scope and current checkpoint project/revision/hash greater than591. Existing global attempt or R4 run blocks replay; exclusive mkdir and flushed CONSUMED precede Popen. Independent in-memory tests cover stale checkpoint, wrong project, bool limits, template status, nonpublic scope, source drift, traversal, existing attempts and consumption failures.
